takeaway: Muscarinic receptors are found in most involuntary organs; nicotinic receptors are at the skeletal neuromuscular junction and in autonomic ganglia. Both respond to acetylcholine.

question.text: Which of the following statements relating to cholinergic receptors is true?

answer.text: Muscarinic receptors are present in most involuntary organs.

lines.text: Acetylcholine is the transmitter of all somatic motor neurons, preganglionic neurons, and most postganglionic parasympathetic neurons.
Its effect depends on the receptor type: nicotinic or muscarinic.
Nicotinic receptors sit at the neuromuscular junction of skeletal muscle, and in autonomic ganglia.
They are named for nicotine, from tobacco.
Muscarinic receptors are named for muscarine, from poisonous mushrooms.
They are found in most involuntary organs: the gut, the bladder, the heart.
Not skeletal muscle. That is nicotinic territory.
lines.say: Not skeletal muscle. (laugh) That is nicotinic territory.

lines.text: So the true statement: muscarinic receptors are present in most involuntary organs.
